sections_inspected: pp. 18–26, 31; sections “Conceptualizing Power,” “The Relational Power of Elites and Nonelites,” “Organizational Power: Powers to Direct and Coordinate,” and “Ideational Power”
scope_outcomes.criterion: A retained finding requires a substantive passage in which the citing text adopts, builds on, qualifies, disputes, or merely mentions a proposition attributed to Weber.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected passages explicitly attribute propositions about power, organizational domination, bureaucracy, legitimacy, formal and informal power, and consensuality to Weber and position those propositions within the authors’ relational power theory.
limitations: Only the supplied source window and the specified sections were assessed; this is not a determination about the entire chapter or the authors’ complete work.
The source cites Weber alongside other thinkers, so some broader claims cannot be attributed to Weber alone.
